jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.description: From the manger in Bethlehem to the empty tomb in Jerusalem and the ascension from the Mount of Olives.

stops.name: Bethlehem
stops.description: Born in a manger during Caesar Augustus's census; visited by shepherds and later by magi from the east.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.description: Presented at the temple on the eighth day; recognized by Simeon and Anna as the consolation of Israel.

stops.name: Egypt
stops.description: The Holy Family fled here under Joseph's dream to escape Herod's massacre of the children of Bethlehem.

stops.name: Nazareth
stops.description: Childhood and youth in the Galilean town; learned the carpenter's trade in Joseph's shop and grew in wisdom and stature.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.description: At twelve, lingered behind in the temple courts questioning the teachers — 'did you not know I must be about my Father's business?'

stops.name: The Jordan River (Bethany beyond the Jordan)
stops.description: Baptized by John; the heavens opened and the voice declared him the beloved Son.

stops.name: The Judean Wilderness
stops.description: Forty days of fasting and temptation by Satan among the wild beasts of the desert.

stops.name: Cana
stops.description: Turned water into wine at a wedding feast — the first of his signs revealing his glory.

stops.name: Capernaum
stops.description: Made this lakeside town his ministry headquarters; healed Peter's mother-in-law, the centurion's servant, the paralytic let down through the roof.

stops.name: Sea of Galilee
stops.description: Called the first disciples from their nets; calmed the storm; walked on the water; preached the parables from a boat.

stops.name: The Mount of Beatitudes
stops.description: Preached the Sermon on the Mount above the Sea of Galilee — the Beatitudes, the Lord's Prayer, the lilies of the field.

stops.name: Nain
stops.description: Raised the widow's only son from his bier as the funeral procession was carried out of the city gate.

stops.name: Caesarea Philippi
stops.description: At the rock of Pan, Peter confessed him as the Christ; Jesus first spoke openly of his coming death and resurrection.

stops.name: Mount Tabor
stops.description: Traditional site of the Transfiguration; appeared in shining glory with Moses and Elijah before Peter, James, and John.

stops.name: Samaria (Sychar)
stops.description: At Jacob's well, conversed with the Samaritan woman; the city believed because of her testimony.

stops.name: Bethany
stops.description: Often guest of Martha, Mary, and Lazarus; raised Lazarus from the tomb after four days.

stops.name: Jericho
stops.description: Healed blind Bartimaeus by the road and called Zacchaeus down from the sycamore-fig to share his table.

stops.name: The Mount of Olives
stops.description: Wept over Jerusalem; rode down its slope on Palm Sunday; gave the Olivet discourse to his disciples.

stops.name: Jerusalem (Triumphal Entry)
stops.description: Entered the city on a colt to the cries of Hosanna and palm branches; cleansed the temple of moneychangers.

stops.name: The Upper Room
stops.description: Washed the disciples' feet and inaugurated the Lord's Supper on the night he was betrayed.

stops.name: The Garden of Gethsemane
stops.description: Prayed in agony — 'not my will but yours be done' — and was betrayed with a kiss.

stops.name: House of Annas and Caiaphas
stops.description: Tried before the high priests by night; condemned for blasphemy; struck and mocked by the guards.

stops.name: Pilate's Praetorium
stops.description: Brought before Pontius Pilate, sent to Herod Antipas and back; scourged and sentenced to crucifixion.

stops.name: Golgotha
stops.description: Crucified between two criminals; cried out 'it is finished' and gave up his spirit at the ninth hour.

stops.name: The Garden Tomb
stops.description: Buried in Joseph of Arimathea's new tomb; on the third day Mary Magdalene found it open and empty.

stops.name: The Road to Emmaus
stops.description: Walked with two disciples after the resurrection and was made known to them in the breaking of bread.

stops.name: Sea of Galilee (post-resurrection)
stops.description: Appeared on the shore at dawn; the miraculous catch of fish; restored Peter with three questions of love.

stops.name: The Mount of Olives (Ascension)
stops.description: After forty days he was taken up into heaven from this mountain; two men in white promised his return.

moses.name: Moses
moses.description: From Pharaoh's house in Egypt to the edge of the promised land overlooking Jericho from Mount Nebo.

stops.name: Goshen
stops.description: Born to Hebrew slaves in the eastern Egyptian delta during Pharaoh's edict to kill the Hebrew boys.

stops.name: The Nile
stops.description: Placed in a pitch-sealed basket among the reeds where Pharaoh's daughter came down to bathe and rescued him.

stops.name: Memphis (Pharaoh's House)
stops.description: Raised in the royal court of Egypt as the son of Pharaoh's daughter; learned all the wisdom of the Egyptians.

stops.name: Midian
stops.description: Fled here after killing an Egyptian overseer; tended Jethro's flocks for forty years and married Zipporah.

stops.name: Mount Horeb (the burning bush)
stops.description: Met God in the flame of the bush that was not consumed; received the divine name and the commission to return to Egypt.

stops.name: Egypt (the plagues)
stops.description: Confronted Pharaoh through ten plagues — blood, frogs, gnats, flies, livestock, boils, hail, locusts, darkness, death of the firstborn.

stops.name: Rameses (Exodus departure)
stops.description: Led six hundred thousand Israelite men plus women and children out of slavery on the night of Passover.

stops.name: Succoth
stops.description: First wilderness encampment after leaving Rameses; pillar of cloud by day and fire by night went before them.

stops.name: The Red Sea crossing
stops.description: God parted the sea with a strong east wind; Israel crossed on dry ground while Pharaoh's army was drowned behind them.

stops.name: Marah
stops.description: Found bitter water; the Lord showed Moses a piece of wood to cast in and the water became sweet.

stops.name: Elim
stops.description: Twelve springs and seventy palm trees; the Israelites camped there beside the water.

stops.name: The Wilderness of Sin
stops.description: Grumbled for food; God sent manna in the morning and quail in the evening for the forty wilderness years.

stops.name: Rephidim
stops.description: Water from the struck rock; battle with Amalek won while Aaron and Hur held up Moses's arms.

stops.name: Mount Sinai
stops.description: Received the Ten Commandments and the Law in fire and smoke; the people made the golden calf at the foot of the mountain.

stops.name: Kadesh Barnea
stops.description: Sent twelve spies into Canaan from this oasis; the people refused to enter and were sentenced to forty wilderness years.

stops.name: The Wilderness of Paran
stops.description: Forty years of wandering in this desert south of Canaan; the whole generation that left Egypt died here except Caleb and Joshua.

stops.name: The Plains of Moab
stops.description: Israel encamped opposite Jericho on the east side of the Jordan; Moses delivered the speeches recorded in Deuteronomy.

stops.name: Mount Nebo
stops.description: Climbed Pisgah to see the land he could not enter; died there at a hundred and twenty and was buried by the Lord in an unknown grave.

paul.name: Paul
paul.description: Three missionary journeys from Antioch to the heart of the Roman world, ending under house arrest in Rome.

stops.name: Tarsus
stops.description: Birthplace; Roman citizen of a Cilician trading city, trained in Greek learning and Pharisaic Judaism.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.description: Studied under Gamaliel; consented to Stephen's stoning; persecuted the early church house by house.

stops.name: The Damascus Road
stops.description: Struck by a light from heaven and blinded; the risen Christ asked, 'why do you persecute me?'

stops.name: Damascus
stops.description: Ananias restored his sight and baptized him; he preached Christ in the synagogues and was let down the wall in a basket to escape.

stops.name: Arabia
stops.description: Withdrew into the Nabatean kingdom for a time of seclusion and reflection before returning to Damascus.

stops.name: Jerusalem (first visit)
stops.description: Three years after his conversion; Barnabas brought him to the apostles when they were still afraid of him.

stops.name: Tarsus (years of obscurity)
stops.description: Sent home for safety; spent perhaps a decade in his native city before Barnabas came to find him.

stops.name: Antioch of Syria
stops.description: Taught with Barnabas for a year in the city where the disciples were first called Christians.

stops.name: Seleucia
stops.description: Antioch's port; embarkation point for the first missionary journey with Barnabas and John Mark.

stops.name: Salamis, Cyprus
stops.description: Landed in Cyprus and preached in the synagogues of Salamis on the eastern shore.

stops.name: Paphos, Cyprus
stops.description: Confronted the magician Bar-Jesus and converted the Roman proconsul Sergius Paulus.

stops.name: Perga
stops.description: Landed on the mainland of Asia Minor; John Mark left them here and returned to Jerusalem.

stops.name: Pisidian Antioch
stops.description: Preached a long synagogue sermon tracing the gospel from David; the Gentiles begged to hear it again the next Sabbath.

stops.name: Iconium
stops.description: Spoke boldly; the city split; Paul and Barnabas fled when a plot to stone them was uncovered.

stops.name: Lystra
stops.description: Healed a man lame from birth; the crowds tried to offer sacrifices to them as Hermes and Zeus, then stoned Paul and left him for dead.

stops.name: Derbe
stops.description: Easternmost point of the first journey; many disciples made before turning back to strengthen the new churches.

stops.name: Jerusalem Council
stops.description: Defended Gentile freedom from circumcision at the council that established the gospel's reach beyond Judaism.

stops.name: Antioch of Syria (second journey)
stops.description: Parted from Barnabas over John Mark; took Silas and went through Syria and Cilicia strengthening the churches.

stops.name: Lystra (joined by Timothy)
stops.description: Met Timothy, son of Eunice; circumcised him for the sake of the synagogues and took him on the journey.

stops.name: Troas
stops.description: Saw the vision of the man of Macedonia by night — 'come over and help us.' Boarded ship for Europe.

stops.name: Neapolis
stops.description: First landing on European soil; port city for nearby Philippi.

stops.name: Philippi
stops.description: Lydia of Thyatira was baptized at the river outside the gate; Paul and Silas were jailed, sang at midnight, and an earthquake broke the stocks.

stops.name: Thessalonica
stops.description: Three Sabbaths in the synagogue; many believed but a mob attacked the house of Jason and ran them out of the city.

stops.name: Berea
stops.description: More noble than Thessalonica — examined the scriptures daily to test what they heard; many believed before the Thessalonians arrived to stir up the crowds.

stops.name: Athens
stops.description: Provoked by the city's idols; debated in the synagogue and the agora; preached on Mars Hill from the altar to an unknown god.

stops.name: Corinth
stops.description: Stayed eighteen months with Aquila and Priscilla, fellow tentmakers; founded a church; wrote 1 and 2 Thessalonians from here.

stops.name: Cenchreae
stops.description: Corinth's eastern port; Paul cut his hair here under a vow before sailing for Ephesus.

stops.name: Ephesus (brief first visit)
stops.description: Left Priscilla and Aquila there; promised to return; sailed for Caesarea and Jerusalem.

stops.name: Caesarea Maritima
stops.description: Landed and went up to greet the church in Jerusalem before returning to Antioch — end of the second journey.

stops.name: Ephesus (third journey)
stops.description: Two years of daily lectures in the hall of Tyrannus; the riot of the silversmiths in the theater; the burning of magic books.

stops.name: Troas (raising Eutychus)
stops.description: Preached till midnight; a young man named Eutychus fell asleep, fell from a third-story window, and was raised up.

stops.name: Miletus
stops.description: Met the Ephesian elders on the shore; warned them of wolves to come; knelt with them on the beach and wept at parting.

stops.name: Tyre
stops.description: Stayed seven days; disciples warned him through the Spirit not to go to Jerusalem; knelt with them on the beach.

stops.name: Caesarea Maritima
stops.description: Stayed with Philip the Evangelist; Agabus bound himself with Paul's belt and prophesied his arrest.

stops.name: Jerusalem (arrest)
stops.description: Took Nazarite vows in the temple; a mob attacked him as a defiler; the Roman tribune arrested him.

stops.name: Caesarea Maritima (imprisonment)
stops.description: Held two years under Felix; defended himself before Festus and Agrippa; appealed to Caesar.

stops.name: Fair Havens, Crete
stops.description: Paul warned against sailing on; the centurion overruled him and the ship was driven by a Euroclydon storm.

stops.name: Malta
stops.description: Shipwrecked on Malta; bitten by a viper but unharmed; healed the father of Publius and many sick on the island.

stops.name: Syracuse
stops.description: Three days in this Sicilian port on the voyage's final leg.

stops.name: Rhegium
stops.description: Stopped at the toe of Italy; favorable south wind carried them on the next day.

stops.name: Puteoli
stops.description: Landed in this Italian port and found brothers who welcomed him; stayed with them seven days.

stops.name: The Forum of Appius and Three Taverns
stops.description: Brothers came out from Rome to meet him on the Appian Way; seeing them he thanked God and took courage.

stops.name: Rome
stops.description: Two years of house arrest in his own rented quarters; preached the kingdom of God boldly to all who came; wrote Ephesians, Philippians, Colossians, Philemon.

abraham.name: Abraham
abraham.description: From Ur of the Chaldees to a grave in the promised land; the journey that became the founding pilgrimage of three faiths.

stops.name: Ur of the Chaldees
stops.description: Born in this Sumerian city of moon-worship; left it with Terah at God's call.

stops.name: Haran
stops.description: Sojourned with Terah on the upper Euphrates until his father died, then resumed the journey to Canaan.

stops.name: Shechem (the oak of Moreh)
stops.description: First arrival in Canaan; the Lord appeared and said, 'to your offspring I will give this land.' Built his first altar.

stops.name: Bethel
stops.description: Pitched his tent between Bethel and Ai; built an altar and called on the name of the Lord.

stops.name: The Negev
stops.description: Moved south through the dry country during a famine in the land of Canaan.

stops.name: Egypt
stops.description: Took refuge during famine; passed Sarah off as his sister; Pharaoh took her into his house but the Lord struck the household with plagues.

stops.name: Bethel (return)
stops.description: Returned to the place of his first altar; called again on the name of the Lord.

stops.name: Hebron (the oaks of Mamre)
stops.description: Settled by the great trees of Mamre after parting from Lot; built an altar to the Lord.

stops.name: Dan
stops.description: Led three hundred and eighteen trained men of his household this far north to rescue Lot from the four eastern kings.

stops.name: Salem (meeting Melchizedek)
stops.description: On the return from rescuing Lot, met Melchizedek priest of God Most High in the King's Valley; gave him a tenth of the spoils.

stops.name: Hebron (the covenant)
stops.description: The Lord cut covenant with him between halved animals; the smoking firepot passed through; the promise of land and seed sealed.

stops.name: Mamre (three visitors)
stops.description: Three men appeared at the door of the tent in the heat of the day; the promise of Isaac was given and Sodom's coming destruction foretold.

stops.name: Gerar
stops.description: Sojourned among the Philistines; Abimelech took Sarah into his house before God warned him in a dream.

stops.name: Beersheba
stops.description: Made covenant with Abimelech and planted a tamarisk tree; called on the everlasting God; Isaac was born and weaned here.

stops.name: Mount Moriah
stops.description: Bound Isaac on the altar and raised the knife; God provided a ram caught in the thicket and renewed the covenant under oath.

stops.name: Hebron (death and burial)
stops.description: Bought the cave of Machpelah from Ephron the Hittite for four hundred shekels; buried Sarah, and was himself buried there at a hundred and seventy-five.

noah.name: Noah
noah.description: From the antediluvian world to the mountains of Ararat where the ark came to rest.

stops.name: The antediluvian world
stops.description: Built the ark for over a century while preaching righteousness to a generation that did not listen.

stops.name: The ark
stops.description: Took refuge with his family and pairs of every creature; the fountains of the deep broke open and the windows of heaven were opened.

stops.name: Mount Ararat
stops.description: The ark came to rest on this mountain in eastern Anatolia; Noah built an altar and offered burnt sacrifices on the dry earth.

enoch.name: Enoch
enoch.description: Walked with God for three hundred and sixty-five years and was not, for God took him.

stops.name: The antediluvian world
stops.description: Walked with God in the days before the flood; fathered Methuselah and was taken without seeing death.

melchizedek.name: Melchizedek
melchizedek.description: Priest-king of Salem who blessed Abraham with bread and wine.

stops.name: Salem
stops.description: King of Salem and priest of God Most High; brought out bread and wine to bless Abraham in the King's Valley.

lot.name: Lot
lot.description: From Ur to a cave in the hills of Moab — a long descent that ended at the edge of Sodom's ash.

stops.name: Ur of the Chaldees
stops.description: Left with his uncle Abraham on the long journey north and west to Canaan.

stops.name: Haran
stops.description: Lingered with Terah until Abraham resumed the journey south to Canaan.

stops.name: Bethel
stops.description: Settled with Abraham between Bethel and Ai until the flocks grew too large for shared pasture.

stops.name: The Jordan Valley
stops.description: Chose the well-watered plain like the garden of the Lord and pitched his tent toward Sodom.

stops.name: Sodom
stops.description: Moved into the city; was captured in the war of the four kings against the five and rescued by Abraham.

stops.name: Zoar
stops.description: Fled with his daughters to this small city as Sodom and Gomorrah burned; his wife looked back and became a pillar of salt.

stops.name: The hills of Moab
stops.description: Hid with his two daughters in a cave; the daughters bore Moab and Ben-Ammi, ancestors of the Moabite and Ammonite nations.

sarah.name: Sarah
sarah.description: Followed Abraham out of Ur and through forty years of wandering; bore Isaac at ninety.

stops.name: Ur of the Chaldees
stops.description: Born and married to Abraham in this Sumerian city; left it at his call.

stops.name: Haran
stops.description: Sojourned on the upper Euphrates with the household of Terah.

stops.name: Shechem
stops.description: Arrived in Canaan with Abraham; passed by the oak of Moreh.

stops.name: Egypt
stops.description: Taken into Pharaoh's house when Abraham called her his sister; restored by Pharaoh after plagues.

stops.name: Hebron (the oaks of Mamre)
stops.description: Settled here; gave Hagar to Abraham; laughed in the tent when told she would bear a son.

stops.name: Gerar
stops.description: Taken into Abimelech's house when Abraham again called her his sister.

stops.name: Beersheba
stops.description: Bore Isaac at ninety; sent Hagar and Ishmael away after the weaning feast.

stops.name: Hebron (burial)
stops.description: Died at a hundred and twenty-seven; buried in the cave of Machpelah, the first piece of the promised land owned by Abraham.

hagar.name: Hagar
hagar.description: Egyptian handmaid found twice in the wilderness by the God who sees.

stops.name: Egypt
stops.description: Born here and taken by Sarah from Pharaoh's household as a maidservant.

stops.name: Hebron
stops.description: Given to Abraham as a surrogate; conceived Ishmael.

stops.name: The Wilderness of Shur
stops.description: Fled south toward Egypt; the angel of the Lord found her by a spring on the road and sent her back.

stops.name: Beer-lahai-roi
stops.description: Named the well 'the God who sees me' after her encounter with the angel; bore Ishmael.

stops.name: The Wilderness of Beersheba
stops.description: Cast out a second time with bread and water; sat down at a distance from her dying son; God opened her eyes to a well.

stops.name: The Wilderness of Paran
stops.description: Settled here with Ishmael; found him an Egyptian wife from her own people.

isaac.name: Isaac
isaac.description: Walked the southern lands his father had walked — between Beersheba, Gerar, and the wells of his father.

stops.name: Beersheba
stops.description: Born and weaned here; Abraham held a great feast on the day of his weaning.

stops.name: Mount Moriah
stops.description: Carried the wood up the mountain on his back; was bound on the altar; saved by the ram in the thicket.

stops.name: Beer-lahai-roi
stops.description: Lived here after Sarah's death; went out to meditate in the fields at evening when his servant brought Rebekah.

stops.name: Gerar
stops.description: Sojourned with Abimelech king of the Philistines during a famine; sowed and reaped a hundredfold.

stops.name: The Valley of Gerar
stops.description: Re-dug the wells his father had dug — Esek, Sitnah, Rehoboth — that the Philistines had stopped up.

stops.name: Beersheba (covenant)
stops.description: The Lord appeared and renewed the covenant; built an altar; made peace with Abimelech.

stops.name: Hebron
stops.description: Died at a hundred and eighty; buried by his sons Esau and Jacob in the cave of Machpelah.

rebekah.name: Rebekah
rebekah.description: From the well in Paddan Aram to a tent in the Negev — and into the centerpiece of the patriarchal narrative.

stops.name: Paddan Aram
stops.description: Born and raised in the household of her brother Laban; came to the well that day at the right hour.

stops.name: The road to Canaan
stops.description: Left her family on a single day's notice; traveled with Abraham's servant by camel caravan.

stops.name: Beer-lahai-roi
stops.description: Met Isaac walking in the fields at evening; he loved her and was comforted after his mother's death.

stops.name: Gerar
stops.description: Like Sarah before her, taken to be called Isaac's sister; saw through by Abimelech.

stops.name: Hebron
stops.description: Engineered Jacob's stolen blessing and sent him into exile; buried in the cave of Machpelah.

jacob.name: Jacob
jacob.description: From Beersheba to Haran to Bethel and at last to Egypt — the long restless circuit of Israel.

stops.name: Beersheba
stops.description: Born clutching Esau's heel; bought the birthright for a bowl of red stew; stole the blessing by deceit.

stops.name: Bethel (Jacob's ladder)
stops.description: Slept with a stone for a pillow on his flight north; saw the ladder reaching to heaven and the Lord standing above it.

stops.name: Haran
stops.description: Served Laban twenty years; was tricked into marrying Leah first; worked another seven for Rachel; fathered eleven sons and a daughter.

stops.name: Mizpah (covenant heap)
stops.description: Parted from Laban under a covenant heap of stones; the Lord watch between us when we are absent one from another.

stops.name: Mahanaim
stops.description: Met by two camps of angels — God's host — as he came back into Canaan; named the place 'two camps.'

stops.name: Peniel (wrestling)
stops.description: Wrestled the man through the night by the Jabbok; his hip was put out of joint; received the new name Israel.

stops.name: Reunion with Esau
stops.description: Met his brother with seven bowings; Esau ran to meet him, embraced him, and they wept together.

stops.name: Shechem
stops.description: Bought a piece of land and pitched his tent; Dinah was defiled here and his sons took bloody revenge.

stops.name: Bethel (return)
stops.description: Buried the household gods under the oak and returned to build the altar at the place of his vision.

stops.name: Bethlehem (Rachel's death)
stops.description: Rachel died in childbirth on the road; he set a pillar over her grave that is the grave of Rachel to this day.

stops.name: Hebron
stops.description: Settled with Isaac in his old age; received the news of Joseph's death and tore his garments.

stops.name: Beersheba (sacrifices on the way to Egypt)
stops.description: Offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac before going down to Egypt; God spoke to him in visions of the night.

stops.name: Goshen, Egypt
stops.description: Settled with his family in the best of the land; presented to Pharaoh; blessed the king of Egypt.

stops.name: Hebron (burial)
stops.description: Died at a hundred and forty-seven; embalmed in Egypt and carried back to the cave of Machpelah for burial.

joseph.name: Joseph
joseph.description: From a pit in Dothan to Pharaoh's chariot — the brother sold became the savior of his family.

stops.name: Hebron
stops.description: Born to Rachel in Paddan Aram, raised in his father's household in the Hebron hills; favored son in the coat of many colors.

stops.name: Shechem
stops.description: Sent by Jacob to check on his brothers at pasture; could not find them in the fields.

stops.name: Dothan
stops.description: Found his brothers here; was stripped, thrown into a pit, and sold to Ishmaelite traders bound for Egypt.

stops.name: Egypt (Potiphar's house)
stops.description: Sold to Potiphar, captain of the guard; rose to overseer of the house; falsely accused by Potiphar's wife.

stops.name: Egypt (Pharaoh's prison)
stops.description: Imprisoned for a crime he had not committed; interpreted the dreams of the cupbearer and the baker.

stops.name: Egypt (Pharaoh's court)
stops.description: Brought from the dungeon to interpret Pharaoh's dreams of cows and grain; made second only to Pharaoh in a single day.

stops.name: On (Heliopolis)
stops.description: Given Asenath daughter of Potiphera priest of On as wife; bore Manasseh and Ephraim.

stops.name: Goshen
stops.description: Brought his father and brothers to live in this fertile delta region during the famine years.

stops.name: Shechem (burial)
stops.description: His bones were carried back from Egypt in the Exodus and buried in the field Jacob had bought at Shechem.

joshua.name: Joshua
joshua.description: Moses's apprentice through the wilderness; the general who took Canaan stronghold by stronghold.

stops.name: Egypt
stops.description: Born in slavery; left Egypt with the rest of Israel under Moses.

stops.name: Rephidim (battle of Amalek)
stops.description: First mention in scripture — led Israel in battle against Amalek while Moses raised his hands on the hilltop.

stops.name: Mount Sinai
stops.description: Went up partway with Moses to receive the Law; remained as Moses's attendant for the forty days.

stops.name: Kadesh Barnea (the spies)
stops.description: One of the twelve spies; brought back a faithful report with Caleb; sentenced to wait forty years for the others to die.

stops.name: Plains of Moab
stops.description: Commissioned by Moses as his successor before the people; received the mantle 'be strong and courageous.'

stops.name: Shittim
stops.description: Israel's last encampment east of the Jordan; sent two spies into Jericho who were sheltered by Rahab.

stops.name: The Jordan crossing
stops.description: The waters rose up in a heap when the priests bearing the ark stepped in; Israel crossed on dry ground.

stops.name: Gilgal
stops.description: First camp inside Canaan; circumcised the wilderness generation and kept the Passover; twelve stones from the Jordan set up here.

stops.name: Jericho
stops.description: Encircled the city for seven days; the walls fell at the trumpet blast on the seventh day; Rahab's household was spared.

stops.name: Ai
stops.description: Defeated at first because of Achan's sin; took the city by ambush after the cherem was executed; built an altar on Mount Ebal.

stops.name: Gibeon
stops.description: The Gibeonites tricked him into a covenant of peace with stale bread; he kept the oath when they were discovered.

stops.name: The Valley of Aijalon
stops.description: Defeated the five Amorite kings; sun stood still over Gibeon and moon over Aijalon for almost a whole day.

stops.name: Hazor
stops.description: Defeated Jabin king of Hazor and the northern coalition by the waters of Merom; burned the city with fire.

stops.name: Shiloh
stops.description: Set up the tabernacle here and divided the land by lot among the seven remaining tribes.

stops.name: Shechem (covenant renewal)
stops.description: Gathered all Israel to renew the covenant; set up a great stone under the oak by the sanctuary of the Lord.

stops.name: Timnath-serah
stops.description: Settled and died here in the hill country of Ephraim, his tribal inheritance, at a hundred and ten.

caleb.name: Caleb
caleb.description: From the assembly at Kadesh to the hills of Hebron — courage outlasting an entire generation.

stops.name: Egypt
stops.description: Of the tribe of Judah; left Egypt with Israel as a young man.

stops.name: Kadesh Barnea
stops.description: One of the twelve spies sent into Canaan; brought back a faithful report and was nearly stoned by the assembly.

stops.name: The Wilderness of Paran
stops.description: Wandered with the rest of Israel forty years; outlived his whole generation but Joshua.

stops.name: Gilgal
stops.description: At eighty-five came to Joshua and asked for the hill country promised him: 'give me this mountain.'

stops.name: Hebron
stops.description: Drove out the three sons of Anak — Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai — and took the city as his inheritance.

stops.name: Debir (Kiriath-sepher)
stops.description: Offered his daughter Achsah to whoever captured this city; Othniel his nephew took it and became Israel's first judge.

aaron.name: Aaron
aaron.description: Spokesman before Pharaoh; first high priest; died on Mount Hor.

stops.name: Egypt
stops.description: Born in Egypt three years before Moses; spoke for him before Pharaoh through the plagues.

stops.name: Mount Sinai
stops.description: Yielded to the people and made the golden calf while Moses was on the mountain; consecrated as high priest in his own right.

stops.name: Rephidim
stops.description: Held up Moses's hands with Hur as Joshua fought Amalek in the valley below.

stops.name: The Wilderness
stops.description: Mediator between Moses and the people; his sons Nadab and Abihu offered strange fire and were consumed.

stops.name: Meribah at Kadesh
stops.description: Stood with Moses when he struck the rock; for that act both were forbidden to enter the land.

stops.name: Mount Hor
stops.description: Climbed the mountain with Moses and Eleazar; his garments were placed on Eleazar; he died there at a hundred and twenty-three.

miriam.name: Miriam
miriam.description: From the reeds of the Nile to the wilderness of Kadesh.

stops.name: Goshen
stops.description: Born in Hebrew slavery in eastern Egypt; older sister of Moses and Aaron.

stops.name: The Nile
stops.description: Watched Moses's basket among the reeds and offered Pharaoh's daughter a Hebrew nurse — her own mother.

stops.name: The Red Sea
stops.description: Took the tambourine and led the women of Israel in the Song of Miriam after the deliverance.

stops.name: Hazeroth
stops.description: Spoke with Aaron against Moses over his Cushite wife; struck with leprosy and quarantined seven days outside the camp.

stops.name: Kadesh Barnea
stops.description: Died here and was buried; Israel had no water in the days that followed.

zipporah.name: Zipporah
zipporah.description: From the well in Midian to the camp at Rephidim.

stops.name: Midian
stops.description: Daughter of Jethro the Midianite priest; one of seven sisters at the well where Moses defended them.

stops.name: The road to Egypt
stops.description: On the road back to Egypt, circumcised her son with a flint to save Moses's life — the bridegroom of blood.

stops.name: Rephidim
stops.description: Brought back to Moses by her father Jethro after the Exodus; reunited with him in the wilderness camp.

rahab.name: Rahab
rahab.description: Hid the spies on a rooftop in Jericho and was spared when the walls came down.

stops.name: Jericho (in the wall)
stops.description: Hid the Israelite spies under stalks of flax on her roof; let them down by a scarlet cord through the window.

stops.name: Jericho (after the fall)
stops.description: Spared with her household when the walls collapsed; brought out and settled among Israel.

stops.name: Bethlehem (line of David)
stops.description: Married Salmon; bore Boaz; entered the line of David and of Jesus.

deborah.name: Deborah
deborah.description: Judged Israel from a palm in Ephraim; rode to victory with Barak in the Kishon valley.

stops.name: The palm of Deborah
stops.description: Sat under this palm between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim and judged the people.

stops.name: Kedesh-Naphtali
stops.description: Summoned Barak from here to muster the tribes of Israel against the Canaanite chariots of Sisera.

stops.name: Mount Tabor
stops.description: Gathered ten thousand men of Naphtali and Zebulun on the mountain before descending into the valley.

stops.name: The Kishon Valley
stops.description: The Lord routed Sisera and his chariots before Israel; the river Kishon swept them away — that ancient river.

gideon.name: Gideon
gideon.description: From the winepress in Ophrah to the chase across the Jordan with three hundred torches.

stops.name: Ophrah
stops.description: Threshing wheat in a winepress when the angel of the Lord called him a mighty man of valor; tore down his father's altar to Baal.

stops.name: The spring of Harod
stops.description: Mustered thirty-two thousand men; the Lord reduced them to three hundred by who lapped water like a dog.

stops.name: The Valley of Jezreel
stops.description: Surrounded the Midianite camp by night with trumpets, torches, and jars; Midian fled in panic and slew each other.

stops.name: The Jordan fords
stops.description: Pursued the fleeing kings Zebah and Zalmunna across the river; men of Succoth and Penuel refused him bread.

stops.name: Karkor
stops.description: Surprised the remnant of Midian east of the Jordan and captured the two kings; punished Succoth and Penuel on his return.

stops.name: Ophrah (death)
stops.description: Returned home; made an ephod from the spoils that became a snare; judged Israel forty years; buried in his father's tomb.

jephthah.name: Jephthah
jephthah.description: From outlaw of Tob to judge of Israel — and a vow he could not take back.

stops.name: Gilead
stops.description: Son of a harlot, driven out by his half-brothers; refused his father's inheritance.

stops.name: The land of Tob
stops.description: Gathered worthless men around him in this remote land east of Gilead; became a brigand chief.

stops.name: Mizpah of Gilead
stops.description: Invited back by the elders to lead against the Ammonites; made his rash vow before going out to battle.

stops.name: Ammon
stops.description: Defeated the Ammonites with great slaughter from Aroer to Minnith; smote twenty cities.

stops.name: Mizpah (the vow)
stops.description: Returned home; his only daughter came out to meet him with timbrels and dances; bewailed her virginity two months in the hills.

stops.name: The Jordan fords
stops.description: Civil war with Ephraim; killed forty-two thousand by the shibboleth test at the river crossings.

samson.name: Samson
samson.description: From Zorah to a Gazan temple — a Nazirite's strength spent in a single act of broken faith and restored.

stops.name: Zorah
stops.description: Born to barren parents under a Nazirite vow from birth; the Spirit of the Lord began to stir him in the camp of Dan.

stops.name: Timnah
stops.description: Saw a Philistine woman he wanted as wife; tore a lion apart with his hands and later found honey in the carcass.

stops.name: Ashkelon
stops.description: Killed thirty Philistine men to pay off the bet on his riddle after his wife betrayed it to his groomsmen.

stops.name: Ramath-lehi
stops.description: Killed a thousand Philistines with the jawbone of a fresh donkey; named the place 'jawbone hill' and 'fountain of him who called.'

stops.name: Gaza (the gates)
stops.description: Went in to a harlot; rose at midnight, tore the city gates from their posts, and carried them up to the hill before Hebron.

stops.name: The Valley of Sorek
stops.description: Loved Delilah here; revealed the secret of his uncut hair; the Philistines came upon him and bound him.

stops.name: Gaza (prison)
stops.description: Eyes gouged out, set to grind grain in a Philistine prison; his hair began to grow back.

stops.name: Gaza (temple of Dagon)
stops.description: Pushed apart the central pillars of Dagon's temple at the great festival and brought the building down on the lords of the Philistines.

ruth.name: Ruth
ruth.description: From Moab to the threshing floor of Boaz — the foreigner who entered the line of David.

stops.name: Moab
stops.description: Born and married into the Israelite family that had fled the famine; widowed without children.

stops.name: The road to Bethlehem
stops.description: Refused to be sent back to her family — 'where you go I will go' — and walked with Naomi to Judah.

stops.name: The fields of Boaz
stops.description: Gleaned barley behind the harvesters; Boaz noticed her, fed her, and ordered the reapers to leave handfuls for her.

stops.name: The threshing floor
stops.description: Lay down at Boaz's feet by Naomi's counsel; he covered her with the corner of his garment as kinsman-redeemer.

stops.name: Bethlehem
stops.description: Married Boaz; bore Obed, the grandfather of David; the women of Bethlehem laid the child on Naomi's lap.

naomi.name: Naomi
naomi.description: From Bethlehem to Moab and back — bitter Mara who returned full.

stops.name: Bethlehem
stops.description: Driven out with her family by famine; left for the fields of Moab.

stops.name: Moab
stops.description: Lost her husband Elimelech and her two sons in ten years; left a widow with two foreign daughters-in-law.

stops.name: The road to Bethlehem
stops.description: Resolved to return home when she heard the famine was past; tried to send her daughters-in-law back to their families.

stops.name: Bethlehem (return)
stops.description: Returned so changed by grief the women barely recognized her; called herself Mara — bitter.

stops.name: Bethlehem (a son born)
stops.description: The women of the town laid Ruth's child Obed on her lap and said, 'a son has been born to Naomi.'

samuel.name: Samuel
samuel.description: From Shiloh's sanctuary to Bethlehem's anointing — Israel's last judge and kingmaker.

stops.name: Ramathaim-zophim
stops.description: Born to Hannah of Elkanah's house in the hill country of Ephraim.

stops.name: Shiloh
stops.description: Weaned and given to Eli at the sanctuary; heard the Lord call his name in the night.

stops.name: Mizpah
stops.description: Gathered Israel for repentance after the ark's return; set up the Ebenezer stone — thus far the Lord has helped us.

stops.name: Gilgal
stops.description: Anointed Saul as king and confirmed him before all Israel; later rebuked him there for offering sacrifice unlawfully.

stops.name: Ramah (circuit)
stops.description: His home and the seat of his ministry; rode an annual circuit through Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah judging Israel.

stops.name: Bethlehem
stops.description: Came under guise of sacrifice; anointed David, the eighth son of Jesse, while still a boy with the sheep.

stops.name: Naioth in Ramah
stops.description: Sheltered the fleeing David among the prophets; the Spirit overcame Saul's messengers and Saul himself.

stops.name: Ramah (death)
stops.description: Died and was buried at his house; all Israel mourned him.

saul.name: Saul
saul.description: From the lost donkeys to the slopes of Mount Gilboa — Israel's first king, last hours.

stops.name: Gibeah of Benjamin
stops.description: Born here; his home throughout his reign; the citadel of his kingdom.

stops.name: Ramah
stops.description: Met Samuel while searching for his father's donkeys; anointed king in private the next morning.

stops.name: Mizpah
stops.description: Chosen by lot before all Israel and presented as king; some despised him but he held his peace.

stops.name: Jabesh-gilead
stops.description: Rescued the city from Nahash the Ammonite by gathering all Israel; renewed his kingship at Gilgal afterward.

stops.name: Michmash
stops.description: Jonathan's daring assault on the Philistine garrison turned the battle; Saul's rash oath nearly cost his son's life.

stops.name: Amalek
stops.description: Defeated Amalek but spared Agag and the best of the spoil; Samuel announced the kingdom would be taken from him.

stops.name: The wilderness of Ziph
stops.description: Pursued David through the wilderness; spared by David in the cave at En Gedi and the camp at Hachilah.

stops.name: Endor
stops.description: Sought out a medium on the eve of his last battle; called up the spirit of Samuel who pronounced his fall.

stops.name: Mount Gilboa
stops.description: Fought his last battle against the Philistines; saw his three sons die; fell on his own sword rather than be taken alive.

jonathan.name: Jonathan
jonathan.description: From the heights of Michmash to the slopes of Gilboa — the prince who loved David more than the throne.

stops.name: Gibeah of Benjamin
stops.description: Born here as crown prince of Saul's small court.

stops.name: Michmash
stops.description: Climbed the rocks of Bozez and Seneh with his armor-bearer and routed the Philistine garrison; the Lord saved by few.

stops.name: Aijalon
stops.description: Pursued the fleeing Philistines down the pass; ate honey in the wood under his father's foolish oath.

stops.name: The wilderness of Ziph
stops.description: Sought out David in the forest and strengthened his hand in God — 'you shall be king, and I shall be next to you.'

stops.name: Mount Gilboa
stops.description: Died in the rout of Saul's army; David's lament — 'your love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women.'

david.name: David
david.description: From the sheep of Bethlehem to the throne of Jerusalem — through caves, wildernesses, and a long restless reign.

stops.name: Bethlehem
stops.description: Born the eighth son of Jesse; anointed in secret by Samuel while still tending the sheep.

stops.name: Saul's court at Gibeah
stops.description: Played the harp to soothe Saul's evil spirit; rose to high command in his army.

stops.name: The Valley of Elah
stops.description: Faced Goliath the Philistine champion with five smooth stones from the brook; struck him with one.

stops.name: Ramah (Naioth)
stops.description: Fled here to Samuel when Saul tried to kill him; sheltered among the prophets.

stops.name: Nob
stops.description: Took the showbread from Ahimelech and the sword of Goliath; eighty-five priests were slain by Doeg for it.

stops.name: Gath
stops.description: Fled to the Philistine king Achish; feigned madness to escape when recognized as the Israelite champion.

stops.name: The cave of Adullam
stops.description: Gathered four hundred outlaws around himself; his three mighty men broke through the Philistine ranks to bring him water from Bethlehem's well.

stops.name: En Gedi
stops.description: Hid in the caves by the Dead Sea oasis; cut off the corner of Saul's robe in the cave and refused to lift a hand against the Lord's anointed.

stops.name: The wilderness of Maon
stops.description: Nearly trapped by Saul on Sela-hammahlekoth; Saul was called away by a Philistine raid at the last moment.

stops.name: Ziklag
stops.description: Given by Achish king of Gath; raided south of Judah for sixteen months; found burned by Amalekites and rescued the captives.

stops.name: Hebron
stops.description: Anointed king of Judah after Saul's death; ruled seven and a half years from this southern city.

stops.name: Jerusalem (Zion)
stops.description: Took the Jebusite stronghold and made it his capital — the city of David; brought up the ark with dancing.

stops.name: The Valley of Rephaim
stops.description: Defeated the Philistines twice — once head-on, once by circling behind on the Lord's instruction.

stops.name: The rooftop palace
stops.description: Saw Bathsheba bathing; sent for her; arranged Uriah's death; was confronted by the prophet Nathan.

stops.name: Mahanaim
stops.description: Fled across the Jordan when Absalom revolted; received Barzillai's provisions; waited out the battle.

stops.name: Jerusalem (return)
stops.description: Returned to the throne after Absalom's death; reigned forty years in all and was buried in the city of David.

solomon.name: Solomon
solomon.description: Reigned forty years from Jerusalem; built the first temple; sent ships from Ezion-geber to Ophir.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.description: Born to David and Bathsheba; anointed at Gihon Spring; reigned forty years from his father's capital.

stops.name: Gibeon
stops.description: Offered a thousand burnt offerings at the great high place; God appeared in a dream and gave him wisdom.

stops.name: The temple mount
stops.description: Built the first temple in seven years on Mount Moriah; dedicated it with prayer and the cloud of glory.

stops.name: Megiddo
stops.description: Fortified as one of his chariot cities controlling the Jezreel valley and the Via Maris.

stops.name: Hazor
stops.description: Fortified the northern crossroads city against Aram.

stops.name: Gezer
stops.description: Received as dowry when Pharaoh's daughter became his wife; rebuilt as a chariot city.

stops.name: Ezion-geber
stops.description: Built a fleet on the Red Sea coast; ships sailed to Ophir for gold with the help of Hiram of Tyre.

elijah.name: Elijah
elijah.description: From a desert brook to the chariot of fire; the wilderness prophet who would not stay still.

stops.name: Tishbe
stops.description: His hometown in Gilead east of the Jordan; the first verse of his book gives no other genealogy.

stops.name: Samaria (Ahab's court)
stops.description: Announced to Ahab that there would be no rain in Israel except by his word.

stops.name: The brook Cherith
stops.description: Hid here east of the Jordan; ravens brought him bread and meat morning and evening until the brook dried up.

stops.name: Zarephath
stops.description: Lived in the widow's upper room in Phoenicia; her jar of flour and jar of oil never failed; raised her son from death.

stops.name: Mount Carmel
stops.description: Confronted four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal; fire fell from heaven on the drenched altar; ended the drought.

stops.name: Jezreel
stops.description: Outran Ahab's chariot to the city gate as the rain came; fled into the wilderness when Jezebel sent word.

stops.name: Beersheba
stops.description: Sat down under a juniper tree and asked to die; an angel fed him cake and water for the journey ahead.

stops.name: Mount Horeb
stops.description: Forty days' journey to the mountain of God; God passed by not in wind, earthquake, or fire but in the still small voice.

stops.name: Abel-meholah
stops.description: Found Elisha plowing with twelve yoke of oxen and threw his mantle over him.

stops.name: Naboth's vineyard, Jezreel
stops.description: Met Ahab in the stolen vineyard with the word of judgment: in the place where dogs licked Naboth's blood, dogs shall lick yours.

stops.name: The Jordan crossing
stops.description: Struck the river with his rolled mantle; the waters parted and he and Elisha crossed on dry ground.

stops.name: Taken up to heaven
stops.description: A chariot of fire and horses of fire separated them; Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.

elisha.name: Elisha
elisha.description: Successor of Elijah; ranged through Israel from the Jordan to the gates of Damascus.

stops.name: Abel-meholah
stops.description: Called from the plow by Elijah's mantle; slaughtered his oxen, used the plows for firewood, and followed.

stops.name: The Jordan (taking up the mantle)
stops.description: Picked up the fallen mantle after Elijah was taken; struck the water and crossed back over.

stops.name: Jericho
stops.description: Healed the city's bad water by throwing salt into the spring; the waters were healed to this day.

stops.name: Bethel
stops.description: Cursed the jeering youths on the road; two she-bears came out of the woods and tore forty-two of them.

stops.name: Shunem
stops.description: Lodged repeatedly with the wealthy Shunammite woman; promised her a son and later raised the boy from death.

stops.name: Gilgal
stops.description: Made the poisoned stew safe with flour during a famine; multiplied twenty loaves of barley to feed a hundred.

stops.name: The Jordan (Naaman's healing)
stops.description: Sent the Syrian commander Naaman to wash seven times in the river; he came up clean of his leprosy.

stops.name: Dothan
stops.description: Surrounded by Syrian chariots; his servant's eyes were opened to see the hills full of fire; the army was struck with blindness.

stops.name: Samaria
stops.description: Predicted relief from the great siege famine within twenty-four hours; the Syrians fled in panic that night.

stops.name: Damascus
stops.description: Went up to anoint Hazael; wept seeing the evil he would do to Israel; Hazael returned to murder his master Ben-Hadad.

ahab.name: Ahab
ahab.description: From his ivory palace at Samaria to a chariot washed in his own blood.

stops.name: Samaria
stops.description: His capital and ivory palace; the seat of his reign with Jezebel; the chariot pool where dogs licked his blood.

stops.name: Jezreel
stops.description: His winter palace and the site of Naboth's vineyard; here Jezebel sent her false witnesses.

stops.name: Mount Carmel
stops.description: Summoned to the contest with the prophets of Baal; saw the fire fall and the drought break.

stops.name: Aphek
stops.description: Defeated Ben-Hadad of Syria here; spared his life and was rebuked by a prophet for it.

stops.name: Ramoth-gilead
stops.description: Went out disguised in battle to retake this city from Aram; was struck by a stray arrow between the joints of his armor and died.

jezebel.name: Jezebel
jezebel.description: From Sidon to a window in Jezreel; the queen who killed the prophets and was thrown to the dogs.

stops.name: Sidon
stops.description: Daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians; brought her father's gods with her into Israel's court.

stops.name: Samaria
stops.description: Set up the temple of Baal and the Asherah; supported eight hundred and fifty prophets at the royal table.

stops.name: Jezreel (Naboth's vineyard)
stops.description: Wrote letters in Ahab's name; engineered the murder of Naboth so Ahab could take the field.

stops.name: Jezreel (the window)
stops.description: Painted her eyes and adorned her hair when Jehu came up; was thrown down by her own eunuchs; the dogs ate her body.

jonah.name: Jonah
jonah.description: From Joppa to Nineveh by way of the belly of a great fish.

stops.name: Gath-hepher
stops.description: His hometown in Galilee, three miles north of Nazareth.

stops.name: Joppa
stops.description: Went down to the seaport, paid his fare, and boarded a ship bound for Tarshish — the farthest known port west.

stops.name: Tarshish (intended)
stops.description: His intended destination at the western edge of the Mediterranean — likely Tartessus in southern Spain.

stops.name: Lost overboard
stops.description: The Lord hurled a great wind; the sailors cast lots; at his own word they threw him into the raging sea.

stops.name: The belly of the great fish
stops.description: Three days and three nights in the sea creature's belly; prayed from the depths and was vomited onto dry land.

stops.name: Nineveh
stops.description: Walked three days into the great city; preached a five-word sermon; the king came down from his throne in repentance.

stops.name: Outside Nineveh
stops.description: Made a booth east of the city and sat sulking; the Lord prepared a plant and then a worm and asked him about pity.

isaiah.name: Isaiah
isaiah.description: Court prophet of Jerusalem through four kings — from the year King Uzziah died to the siege of Sennacherib.

stops.name: Jerusalem (the temple)
stops.description: Received his vision in the year King Uzziah died — the Lord enthroned, the seraphim, the smoke.

stops.name: The Upper Pool
stops.description: Met King Ahaz at the conduit of the upper pool with his son Shear-jashub; offered the sign of Immanuel.

stops.name: The wall of Jerusalem
stops.description: Stood with Hezekiah during Sennacherib's siege; brought the king's letter into the temple and prayed; the angel struck the Assyrian camp.

jeremiah.name: Jeremiah
jeremiah.description: From Anathoth to a forced exile in Egypt — the weeping prophet who saw Jerusalem fall.

stops.name: Anathoth
stops.description: Born in this priestly village just north of Jerusalem; called as a young man and protested he was only a boy.

stops.name: Jerusalem (the temple gate)
stops.description: Preached the temple sermon in the gate; the priests and prophets sought to kill him; the elders saved him.

stops.name: The valley of Hinnom
stops.description: Broke the potter's flask before the elders; announced this place would be called the valley of slaughter.

stops.name: The stocks at the Upper Benjamin Gate
stops.description: Beaten and put in the stocks by Pashhur the priest; gave him the new name 'Terror on every side.'

stops.name: The court of the guard
stops.description: Confined during the siege; bought the field at Anathoth from his cousin Hanamel as a sign of return.

stops.name: The muddy cistern
stops.description: Lowered with ropes into a cistern to die in the mud; rescued by the Ethiopian Ebed-melech with rags and old clothes.

stops.name: Mizpah
stops.description: Released after Jerusalem's fall; lived with Gedaliah the appointed governor until Ishmael's assassination plot.

stops.name: Tahpanhes, Egypt
stops.description: Carried against his will down into Egypt by the fleeing remnant; hid stones in the brick pavement at Pharaoh's palace.

ezekiel.name: Ezekiel
ezekiel.description: Priest deported to Babylon; saw the throne of God on a chariot and the dry bones rise.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.description: Born here in a priestly family; deported with Jehoiachin in the second deportation of 597 BC.

stops.name: Tel-abib
stops.description: Settled with the exiles by the Chebar canal; sat overwhelmed among them seven days before prophesying.

stops.name: The Chebar canal
stops.description: Received the throne vision — four living creatures, wheels within wheels, the likeness of a man on the sapphire throne.

stops.name: The valley of dry bones
stops.description: Set down in a valley full of dry bones in vision; prophesied and the bones came together with a great rattling.

daniel.name: Daniel
daniel.description: From Jerusalem to the courts of Babylon and Persia — through three kings and a lions' den.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.description: Taken as a young nobleman in the first deportation of 605 BC under Nebuchadnezzar.

stops.name: Babylon (royal academy)
stops.description: Trained in the language and literature of the Chaldeans; refused the king's food and rose in the court.

stops.name: The plain of Dura
stops.description: Where Nebuchadnezzar set up his golden image; his three companions were thrown into the furnace and walked unburnt.

stops.name: Babylon (Belshazzar's feast)
stops.description: Read the handwriting on the wall: mene, mene, tekel, parsin; that very night Belshazzar was killed.

stops.name: Babylon (lions' den)
stops.description: Cast in for praying with his window open toward Jerusalem; the lions' mouths were shut and he emerged unharmed at dawn.

stops.name: Susa (visions)
stops.description: Saw the visions of the ram and the goat by the river Ulai; received Gabriel's answer about the seventy weeks.

stops.name: The Tigris
stops.description: Stood on the bank of the great river and saw a man clothed in linen; received the final apocalyptic visions of his book.

esther.name: Esther
esther.description: From the women's quarter of Susa to the king's banquet — for such a time as this.

stops.name: Susa (the citadel)
stops.description: Orphan raised by Mordecai in the Persian capital; her parents had been carried away from Jerusalem with Jeconiah.

stops.name: Susa (the harem)
stops.description: Taken into Hegai's care for twelve months of beautification before being presented to King Xerxes.

stops.name: Susa (the throne room)
stops.description: Crowned queen in place of Vashti in the seventh year of the king's reign.

stops.name: Susa (the inner court)
stops.description: Approached the king uninvited at the risk of her life; he held out the gold scepter; she invited him and Haman to a banquet.

stops.name: Susa (the banquet)
stops.description: At the second banquet exposed Haman as the enemy of her people; he was hanged on the gallows he had built.

mordecai.name: Mordecai
mordecai.description: From the king's gate at Susa to royal robes and a horse led through the city.

stops.name: Susa (the king's gate)
stops.description: Sat daily at the king's gate; uncovered Bigthana and Teresh's plot to assassinate Xerxes.

stops.name: Susa (in sackcloth)
stops.description: Tore his garments and went out into the city wailing when he heard Haman's decree.

stops.name: Susa (the procession)
stops.description: Led through the streets by Haman in royal robes on the king's horse; returned afterward to the king's gate in sackcloth.

stops.name: Susa (second-in-command)
stops.description: Made second to the king after Haman's fall; wrote with Esther the letter establishing the festival of Purim.

haman.name: Haman
haman.description: From second-in-command of Persia to his own gallows in a single day.

stops.name: Susa (elevation)
stops.description: Elevated above all princes by Xerxes; the king commanded all servants to bow.

stops.name: Susa (the gallows)
stops.description: Built a gallows seventy-five feet high to hang Mordecai; was hanged on it himself the next day.

cyrus.name: Cyrus
cyrus.description: From Anshan to Babylon — the king Isaiah named a century and a half before he was born.

stops.name: Anshan
stops.description: Born to royal blood in the small Persian kingdom of Anshan; founded the Achaemenid empire by unifying Persia.

stops.name: Ecbatana
stops.description: Conquered the Median capital; absorbed the Median kingdom by marriage and force.

stops.name: Babylon
stops.description: Entered Babylon in 539 BC as the gates were opened by the city's priests; honored by Marduk's clergy.

stops.name: Jerusalem (by decree)
stops.description: Issued the decree of 538 BC authorizing Jewish exiles to return and rebuild the temple — Isaiah's anointed king.

ezra.name: Ezra
ezra.description: From Babylon up to Jerusalem with the law in his hand.

stops.name: Babylon
stops.description: Born and trained in the Aaronic line in exile; a scribe skilled in the Law of Moses.

stops.name: The river Ahava
stops.description: Gathered the second wave of returnees and fasted for protection; refused a Persian escort to honor his confession of God's hand.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.description: Arrived in the seventh year of Artaxerxes with treasure for the temple; sat appalled at the people's intermarriage.

stops.name: The Water Gate
stops.description: Read the Law from the wooden platform from morning until midday while the Levites translated; the people wept as they understood.

nehemiah.name: Nehemiah
nehemiah.description: From the cup at Artaxerxes's table to the rebuilt walls of Jerusalem.

stops.name: Susa (the citadel)
stops.description: Cupbearer to Artaxerxes; heard of Jerusalem's broken walls and wept, fasted, and prayed for days.

stops.name: The king's table
stops.description: Asked the king for leave to rebuild; given letters, timber from the royal forest, and a military escort.

stops.name: Jerusalem (the night inspection)
stops.description: Rode out by night past the Valley Gate, the Jackal Well, and the Dung Gate to see what the wall needed.

stops.name: Jerusalem (the walls)
stops.description: Mobilized the people; half worked while half stood guard; finished the walls in fifty-two days.

stops.name: The plain of Ono
stops.description: Refused Sanballat's repeated invitations to meet here — 'I am doing a great work and I cannot come down.'

stops.name: Susa (return to king)
stops.description: Returned to Persia after twelve years and reported back to Artaxerxes.

stops.name: Jerusalem (reforms)
stops.description: Came back to confront foreign marriages, Sabbath-breaking, and a chamber prepared for Tobiah in the temple.

judas-maccabeus.name: Judas Maccabeus
judas-maccabeus.description: From the village altar of Modi'in to the rededicated temple — the hammer of the revolt.

stops.name: Modi'in
stops.description: Hometown of the Hasmonean family; his father Mattathias killed the king's officer at the altar and lit the revolt.

stops.name: Mizpah
stops.description: Gathered Israel here to fast and pray before the first major confrontation with the Seleucids.

stops.name: Emmaus
stops.description: Surprised the Seleucid general Gorgias at dawn and routed his army.

stops.name: Beth-zur
stops.description: Defeated Lysias at this fortress controlling the road from the south to Jerusalem.

stops.name: Jerusalem (the temple)
stops.description: Cleansed the desecrated temple in 164 BC; lit the lampstand for the first eight-day feast of Dedication — Hanukkah.

stops.name: Elasa
stops.description: Fell in battle here in 160 BC against Bacchides; his brothers Jonathan and Simon continued the work.

john-the-baptist.name: John the Baptist
john-the-baptist.description: From the hill country of Judea to the rocks of Machaerus.

stops.name: Ein Karem
stops.description: Traditional site of his birth to Zechariah and Elizabeth in the hill country of Judea.

stops.name: The Judean wilderness
stops.description: Lived in the desert until the day of his appearance; came eating locusts and wild honey in camel hair.

stops.name: The Jordan (Bethany beyond)
stops.description: Baptized those who came from Jerusalem and all Judea; baptized Jesus and saw the dove descend.

stops.name: Aenon near Salim
stops.description: Baptized at this location where there was plenty of water; the disciples discussed his diminishing crowds.

stops.name: Machaerus
stops.description: Imprisoned in Herod Antipas's desert fortress east of the Dead Sea; beheaded at Herodias's request after Salome's dance.

peter.name: Peter
peter.description: From the nets of the Sea of Galilee to the streets of Rome.

stops.name: Bethsaida
stops.description: Born here on the north shore of the Sea of Galilee; brother of Andrew, fisherman by trade.

stops.name: Capernaum
stops.description: Lived here with his wife and mother-in-law; Jesus made his home in the town and healed his mother-in-law of fever.

stops.name: The Jordan (calling)
stops.description: Brought to Jesus by his brother Andrew the day after Jesus's baptism; renamed Cephas, the rock.

stops.name: Sea of Galilee (catching of fish)
stops.description: Left his nets after the miraculous catch and the word 'from now on you will catch men.'

stops.name: Caesarea Philippi
stops.description: Confessed Jesus as the Christ, the Son of the living God; received the keys of the kingdom.

stops.name: Mount Tabor
stops.description: Saw Jesus transfigured; offered to build three booths for Jesus, Moses, and Elijah.

stops.name: Jerusalem (Last Supper)
stops.description: Said he would die with Jesus; was warned of the threefold denial before the cock crowed.

stops.name: Gethsemane
stops.description: Drew his sword and cut off the ear of Malchus the high priest's servant.

stops.name: The high priest's courtyard
stops.description: Denied Jesus three times around the charcoal fire; went out and wept bitterly when the cock crowed.

stops.name: The empty tomb
stops.description: Ran with John to the tomb when Mary brought word; stooped in and saw the linen lying there.

stops.name: Sea of Galilee (restoration)
stops.description: Restored by a charcoal fire on the shore; three times asked 'do you love me?'; commissioned to feed the sheep.

stops.name: Jerusalem (Pentecost)
stops.description: Preached the great sermon at Pentecost; three thousand baptized; the gospel was launched.

stops.name: Joppa
stops.description: Stayed with Simon the tanner; raised Tabitha from death; had the rooftop vision of the unclean animals.

stops.name: Caesarea Maritima
stops.description: Went to the house of Cornelius the centurion; preached and saw the Holy Spirit fall on the Gentiles.

stops.name: Jerusalem (prison)
stops.description: Arrested by Herod Agrippa I; freed by an angel from prison; came to the house of Mary mother of John Mark.

stops.name: Antioch
stops.description: Ate with Gentile believers until the men from James arrived; rebuked by Paul to his face for hypocrisy.

stops.name: Rome (tradition)
stops.description: Tradition has him ministering and martyred in Rome under Nero, crucified upside down on the Vatican hill.

andrew.name: Andrew
andrew.description: From the bank of the Jordan to the cross of Patras — the first-called who first brought others.

stops.name: Bethsaida
stops.description: Born and grew up as a fisherman, brother of Simon Peter.

stops.name: The Jordan (with the Baptist)
stops.description: Disciple of John the Baptist; heard him point out the Lamb of God and followed Jesus.

stops.name: Capernaum
stops.description: Lived with Peter in his Capernaum house; called from his nets with the rest.

stops.name: Bethsaida (the five loaves)
stops.description: Brought the boy with five loaves and two fish to Jesus before the feeding of the five thousand.

stops.name: Patras (tradition)
stops.description: Tradition places his martyrdom on a saltire cross at this Greek port; his name remains on the flag of Scotland.

john-apostle.name: John the Apostle
john-apostle.description: From the boat of Zebedee to the visions of Patmos.

stops.name: Bethsaida
stops.description: Born to Zebedee; a fisherman with his brother James on the Sea of Galilee.

stops.name: Capernaum
stops.description: Called with James from the boat as they mended nets with their father; left him and the hired servants.

stops.name: Mount Tabor (Transfiguration)
stops.description: One of the inner three; saw Jesus transfigured in glory.

stops.name: Jerusalem (Last Supper)
stops.description: Reclined on Jesus's bosom and asked who would betray him.

stops.name: Gethsemane
stops.description: One of the three taken farther into the garden during Jesus's agony.

stops.name: Golgotha
stops.description: Stood at the foot of the cross; entrusted with Mary, the mother of Jesus.

stops.name: The empty tomb
stops.description: Ran with Peter on the resurrection morning; outran him, looked in first, then went in and believed.

stops.name: Jerusalem (the early church)
stops.description: Pillar of the Jerusalem church with Peter; healed the lame man at the Beautiful Gate together.

stops.name: Samaria
stops.description: Sent with Peter to the new Samaritan converts; they prayed and the Holy Spirit fell on them.

stops.name: Ephesus (tradition)
stops.description: Tradition has him settling here in his later years with Mary in his care, leader of the churches of Asia.

stops.name: Patmos
stops.description: Exiled to this rocky island under Domitian; received the visions of the book of Revelation on the Lord's day.

mary-magdalene.name: Mary Magdalene
mary-magdalene.description: From the lakeshore of Magdala to the empty tomb in Jerusalem.

stops.name: Magdala
stops.description: Born here on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee; from her seven demons were cast out.

stops.name: Galilean towns
stops.description: Traveled with Jesus and supported his ministry from her own resources along with other women.

stops.name: Golgotha
stops.description: Stood at the cross when most of the apostles had fled; saw the body taken down.

stops.name: The garden tomb
stops.description: Came at dawn with spices; saw the stone rolled away; turned and recognized the risen Lord at the sound of her name.

martha.name: Martha
martha.description: Anchored in Bethany; one of the steadiest confessions of the Gospels.

stops.name: Bethany
stops.description: Sister of Lazarus and Mary; hosted Jesus repeatedly in her house just over the Mount of Olives from Jerusalem.

lazarus.name: Lazarus
lazarus.description: Called out of the tomb in Bethany.

stops.name: Bethany (the tomb)
stops.description: Buried four days; called by name out of the grave by Jesus's loud cry.

nicodemus.name: Nicodemus
nicodemus.description: Came to Jesus by night; helped bury him in the day.

stops.name: Jerusalem (by night)
stops.description: Came to Jesus at night with the question of being born again.

stops.name: The Sanhedrin
stops.description: Quietly defended Jesus before the council: does our law judge a man without first hearing him?

stops.name: The garden tomb
stops.description: Brought a hundred pounds of myrrh and aloes to help Joseph of Arimathea bury the body.

joseph-arimathea.name: Joseph of Arimathea
joseph-arimathea.description: From Arimathea to a new tomb in the garden — the wealthy secret disciple who buried his Lord.

stops.name: Arimathea
stops.description: His hometown in the hill country of Judea.

stops.name: Pilate's praetorium
stops.description: Went boldly to ask Pilate for the body of Jesus.

stops.name: The garden tomb
stops.description: Wrapped the body in fine linen; laid it in his own new tomb hewn in the rock; rolled the great stone to the entrance.

zacchaeus.name: Zacchaeus
zacchaeus.description: Up a sycamore-fig in Jericho; down to a different life.

stops.name: Jericho (the sycamore)
stops.description: Chief tax collector who ran ahead and climbed the tree to see Jesus pass; came down at Jesus's call.

stops.name: Jericho (his house)
stops.description: Welcomed Jesus joyfully; gave half his goods to the poor and restored fourfold what he had defrauded.

bartimaeus.name: Bartimaeus
bartimaeus.description: Threw off his cloak and saw the road for the first time.

stops.name: Jericho (the road)
stops.description: Sat begging by the road out of Jericho; cried out to the Son of David and was given sight; followed Jesus on the way.

stops.name: Judea (the road)
stops.description: Ran up, knelt, and asked what he must do to inherit eternal life; walked sadly away because he had many possessions.

cornelius.name: Cornelius
cornelius.description: Centurion of the Italian Cohort whose house opened the door of the gospel to the Gentiles.

stops.name: Caesarea Maritima
stops.description: Saw the angel in vision at the ninth hour; sent for Peter at Joppa; the Spirit fell on his household as Peter spoke.

stephen.name: Stephen
stephen.description: First Christian martyr; stoned outside the gates of Jerusalem.

stops.name: Jerusalem (the Hellenist synagogue)
stops.description: Argued with the Synagogue of the Freedmen; none could stand against the wisdom and Spirit by which he spoke.

stops.name: The Sanhedrin
stops.description: Delivered the long defense of Acts 7; saw the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing.

stops.name: Outside the gate
stops.description: Stoned outside the city; prayed for his murderers; Saul of Tarsus held the cloaks.

philip-evangelist.name: Philip the Evangelist
philip-evangelist.description: From Jerusalem to Samaria to the Gaza road — and on up the coast to Caesarea.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.description: Chosen as one of the seven Hellenist deacons to oversee the daily distribution to the widows.

stops.name: Samaria
stops.description: Preached after the scattering of the Jerusalem church; great joy in the city; Simon the magician believed and was baptized.

stops.name: The Gaza road
stops.description: Met the Ethiopian eunuch in his chariot reading Isaiah 53; preached Jesus to him from that very scripture.

stops.name: Azotus
stops.description: Caught up by the Spirit from the eunuch's company and found here; preached through the coastal towns going north.

stops.name: Caesarea Maritima
stops.description: Settled here with his four prophesying daughters; hosted Paul on his way to Jerusalem twenty years later.

barnabas.name: Barnabas
barnabas.description: From Cyprus to Antioch to a missionary partnership and back to Cyprus.

stops.name: Cyprus
stops.description: Born here as Joseph the Levite; sold a field and laid the money at the apostles' feet.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.description: Vouched for the converted Saul of Tarsus when the apostles were afraid of him.

stops.name: Antioch of Syria
stops.description: Sent to investigate the new Gentile mission; was glad and saw the grace of God; went to Tarsus to fetch Saul.

stops.name: Cyprus (first journey)
stops.description: First leg of the first missionary journey with Paul; saw the proconsul Sergius Paulus believe at Paphos.

stops.name: Pisidian Antioch
stops.description: Preached with Paul in the synagogue; turned to the Gentiles when the Jews rejected the word.

stops.name: Lystra
stops.description: Called Zeus by the crowd to Paul's Hermes; barely restrained them from offering sacrifices.

stops.name: Jerusalem (council)
stops.description: Stood with Paul at the council that decided Gentile believers were not bound by circumcision.

stops.name: Cyprus (with John Mark)
stops.description: Split from Paul over John Mark; took his cousin back home to Cyprus to begin again.

silas.name: Silas
silas.description: From the Jerusalem council to the inner cell of the Philippian prison.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.description: A leading man among the brethren; sent with the council's letter to the Gentile churches.

stops.name: Antioch of Syria
stops.description: Delivered the letter to the church; chosen by Paul as second-journey companion after the split with Barnabas.

stops.name: Philippi (the inner cell)
stops.description: Stripped and beaten with rods; thrown into the inner cell with feet in stocks; sang hymns at midnight.

stops.name: Thessalonica
stops.description: Reasoned in the synagogue with Paul for three Sabbaths before the mob attacked Jason's house.

stops.name: Berea
stops.description: Reasoned with the noble-minded Bereans; remained when Paul was sent on ahead to Athens.

stops.name: Corinth
stops.description: Rejoined Paul; co-author with him of the Thessalonian letters.

timothy.name: Timothy
timothy.description: From his mother's house in Lystra to the pastorate at Ephesus.

stops.name: Lystra
stops.description: Born to Eunice and a Greek father; raised in the scriptures by his grandmother Lois and his mother.

stops.name: Iconium
stops.description: Well spoken of by the brothers here and in Lystra when Paul came through and recruited him.

stops.name: Troas
stops.description: With Paul when the vision of the man of Macedonia came.

stops.name: Philippi
stops.description: Part of the first European mission; later sent back to encourage the Philippian church.

stops.name: Thessalonica
stops.description: Sent back from Athens to strengthen and encourage the new church under persecution.

stops.name: Corinth
stops.description: Sent to address troubles in this church; co-sender of several Pauline letters.

stops.name: Ephesus
stops.description: Left here to set the church in order; received the two letters bearing his name.

stops.name: Rome
stops.description: Came to Paul in his final imprisonment at his urgent summons in 2 Timothy.

titus.name: Titus
titus.description: From Antioch to Crete by way of the hardest churches of Paul's mission.

stops.name: Antioch of Syria
stops.description: Greek convert from this church; the uncircumcised test case Paul took to the Jerusalem council.

stops.name: Jerusalem (council)
stops.description: Stood as the living question at the council; not compelled to be circumcised.

stops.name: Ephesus
stops.description: Sent ahead with the painful letter to Corinth from here.

stops.name: Corinth
stops.description: Carried the painful letter and brought back the news of repentance; oversaw the collection for Jerusalem here.

stops.name: Crete
stops.description: Left to set the churches in order and appoint elders in every town; recipient of the letter to Titus.

stops.name: Nicopolis
stops.description: Asked to meet Paul here in Epirus for the winter.

stops.name: Dalmatia
stops.description: Mentioned in 2 Timothy as having gone here; last named destination of his ministry.

lydia.name: Lydia
lydia.description: From Thyatira to the river outside Philippi.

stops.name: Thyatira
stops.description: Her hometown in Asia Minor, famed for its dyers' guild and purple cloth.

stops.name: Philippi (the riverside)
stops.description: Met Paul at the Sabbath prayer place outside the gate by the river; the Lord opened her heart and she was baptized.

aquila.name: Aquila
aquila.description: Tentmaker exiled from Rome who became Paul's longest-running partner in the gospel.

stops.name: Pontus
stops.description: Born to a Jewish family in the Black Sea region of northern Asia Minor.

stops.name: Rome
stops.description: Lived and worked here until expelled with the Jews under Claudius's edict in 49 AD.

stops.name: Corinth
stops.description: Settled here with Priscilla; met Paul the tentmaker and worked with him.

stops.name: Ephesus
stops.description: Moved here with Paul; took Apollos aside with Priscilla to explain the way of God more accurately.

stops.name: Rome (return)
stops.description: Returned to Rome by the time of Romans 16; the church met in their house.

priscilla.name: Priscilla
priscilla.description: Often listed before her husband; teacher of Apollos and partner of Paul.

stops.name: Rome
stops.description: Lived and worked here with Aquila until expelled with the Jews.

stops.name: Corinth
stops.description: Hosted Paul for eighteen months as fellow tentmaker.

stops.name: Ephesus
stops.description: Took Apollos aside in the synagogue and instructed him; led a house church here.

stops.name: Rome (return)
stops.description: Returned to Rome by the time of Romans 16; a church met in her house.

herod-the-great.name: Herod the Great
herod-the-great.description: Built the second temple; massacred the children of Bethlehem.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.description: Capital of his kingdom; site of his rebuilt temple and his desperate paranoia.

stops.name: Caesarea Maritima
stops.description: Built this Roman harbor city from nothing; named it after Caesar Augustus.

stops.name: Masada
stops.description: Built the desert fortress on the cliff above the Dead Sea as a refuge from Jewish revolt.

stops.name: Herodium
stops.description: Built this fortress-palace as his burial site; the artificial mountain near Bethlehem.

stops.name: Bethlehem
stops.description: Ordered the massacre of every boy under two in and around the town.

stops.name: Jericho (winter palace)
