stops.description: Built lavish winter palaces in this warm river-oasis; died here in agony in 4 BC.

herod-antipas.name: Herod Antipas
herod-antipas.description: Tetrarch of Galilee and Perea; beheaded John the Baptist; questioned Jesus.

stops.name: Tiberias
stops.description: Built this lakeside capital on the Sea of Galilee and named it for the emperor Tiberius.

stops.name: Sepphoris
stops.description: His other Galilean capital; rebuilt in the years of Jesus's youth a few miles from Nazareth.

stops.name: Machaerus
stops.description: Held the birthday banquet here at which Salome danced and John the Baptist was beheaded.

stops.name: Jerusalem (trial of Jesus)
stops.description: In the city for Passover when Pilate sent Jesus to him; mocked him in a fine robe and sent him back.

stops.name: Gaul (exile)
stops.description: Banished by Caligula to Lugdunum in Gaul at the urging of his ambitious wife Herodias.

pontius-pilate.name: Pontius Pilate
pontius-pilate.description: From Caesarea to Jerusalem and back — the prefect who washed his hands.

stops.name: Caesarea Maritima
stops.description: Capital of his administration; the city where he normally resided as Roman prefect.

stops.name: Jerusalem (festivals)
stops.description: Came up for major feasts to maintain order; the Antonia fortress overlooked the temple courts.

stops.name: Pilate's praetorium
stops.description: Tried Jesus; washed his hands; ordered the crucifixion at the crowd's insistence.

stops.name: Mount Gerizim
stops.description: Sent troops against Samaritans gathered on this mountain in 36 AD; led to his recall to Rome.

annas.name: Annas
annas.description: Former high priest who pulled strings in the Jerusalem priesthood for a generation.

stops.name: Jerusalem (high priesthood)
stops.description: High priest 6–15 AD; deposed by the Romans but kept de facto authority through his sons and son-in-law.

stops.name: House of Annas
stops.description: Jesus brought to him first after his arrest; questioned about his disciples and teaching; sent bound to Caiaphas.

caiaphas.name: Caiaphas
caiaphas.description: High priest who pronounced it expedient that one man die for the nation.

stops.name: Jerusalem (high priesthood)
stops.description: High priest 18–36 AD; presided over the Sanhedrin during Jesus's ministry and trial.

stops.name: House of Caiaphas
stops.description: Site of the nighttime trial; tore his garments at Jesus's answer and pronounced him a blasphemer.

stops.name: Pilate's praetorium
stops.description: Delivered Jesus to Pilate in the early morning for the Roman sentence.

job.name: Job
job.description: From a great household in Uz to an ash heap and back.

stops.name: The land of Uz
stops.description: His home east of Canaan, perhaps in northern Arabia or Edom; the place of his prosperity and his ruin.

stops.name: The ash heap
stops.description: Sat in ashes scraping his sores with a potsherd while his three friends debated his suffering.

leah.name: Leah
leah.description: From Paddan Aram to a grave at Machpelah.

stops.name: Paddan Aram
stops.description: Born in her father Laban's household; given to Jacob in the wedding-night substitution.

stops.name: Shechem
stops.description: Settled with Jacob near the city after his return to Canaan.

stops.name: Hebron (Machpelah)
stops.description: Buried in the cave of Machpelah — the only one of Jacob's wives laid there.

rachel.name: Rachel
rachel.description: From the well in Paddan Aram to a grave on the road to Bethlehem.

stops.name: Paddan Aram
stops.description: Met Jacob at the well watering her father's sheep.

stops.name: Penuel
stops.description: Crossed back into Canaan with Jacob's caravan after his wrestling at the Jabbok.

stops.name: Bethel
stops.description: Hid the household gods of her father under her saddle and sat on them.

stops.name: On the road to Bethlehem
stops.description: Died in hard labor bearing Benjamin; Jacob set a pillar over her grave.

dinah.name: Dinah
dinah.description: The daughter of Jacob defiled at Shechem.

stops.name: Shechem
stops.description: Went out to visit the women of the land; was taken and violated by Shechem son of Hamor.

tamar.name: Tamar
tamar.description: From the road to Timnah to a place in the line of the Messiah.

stops.name: Adullam
stops.description: Lived in Judah's household as the widow of Er and then of Onan.

stops.name: Enaim (the gate)
stops.description: Veiled herself and sat at the gate on the road Judah took to his sheep-shearing.

stops.name: Bethlehem (the messianic line)
stops.description: Bore Perez and Zerah to Judah; entered the line of David through Perez.

eli.name: Eli
eli.description: Forty years at the sanctuary of Shiloh.

stops.name: Shiloh
stops.description: Served as priest and judge at the tabernacle; raised Samuel; fell from his seat at the news of the ark's capture.

hannah.name: Hannah
hannah.description: From the hill country of Ephraim to Shiloh and back, year after year.

stops.name: Ramathaim-zophim
stops.description: Her home in the hill country of Ephraim with her husband Elkanah.

stops.name: Shiloh
stops.description: Made the annual pilgrimage to the sanctuary; vowed her son to the Lord and gave him into Eli's care after weaning.

bathsheba.name: Bathsheba
bathsheba.description: From a rooftop in Jerusalem to the queen mother's throne.

stops.name: Jerusalem (rooftop)
stops.description: Seen by David from his rooftop while her husband Uriah was at war.

stops.name: Jerusalem (palace)
stops.description: Bore Solomon to David; with Nathan secured his accession to the throne; took her seat at her son's right hand.

absalom.name: Absalom
absalom.description: From Hebron's rebellion to a stranded mule in the forest of Ephraim.

stops.name: Hebron
stops.description: Born here during David's reign at Hebron; raised the banner of revolt here.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.description: Avenged Tamar by killing Amnon at his sheep-shearing feast; later stood at the city gate stealing the hearts of Israel.

stops.name: Geshur
stops.description: Fled into exile at his grandfather Talmai's court for three years after Amnon's murder.

stops.name: The forest of Ephraim
stops.description: Battle joined here; his hair caught in an oak; Joab killed him against David's orders.

joel.name: Joel
joel.description: Prophet in Judah of locusts and the day of the Lord.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.description: Prophesied to the priests and people after a locust plague; promised the outpouring of the Spirit.

amos.name: Amos
amos.description: From Tekoa in Judah to the royal sanctuary at Bethel.

stops.name: Tekoa
stops.description: Shepherd and dresser of sycamores from this Judean village ten miles south of Jerusalem.

stops.name: Bethel
stops.description: Sent north to the royal sanctuary; confronted by Amaziah the priest and ordered back to Judah.

stops.name: Samaria
stops.description: Pronounced judgment on the wealthy of the northern capital who slept on ivory beds.

hosea.name: Hosea
hosea.description: Prophet to the northern kingdom who married Gomer.

stops.name: Samaria
stops.description: Prophesied in the northern capital through the last decades before the Assyrian fall.

stops.name: Jezreel
stops.description: Named his first son for this valley; the place of judgment to come on the house of Jehu.

micah.name: Micah
micah.description: Country prophet from the Judean foothills.

stops.name: Moresheth-gath
stops.description: His hometown in the Shephelah; spoke from the perspective of the small towns under threat.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.description: Prophesied against the urban elite who built Zion with blood; foretold a ruler from Bethlehem.

stops.name: Elkosh
stops.description: His traditional hometown in Judah.

stops.name: Nineveh
stops.description: The Assyrian capital whose fall he announced in his bitter poem; destroyed in 612 BC.

habakkuk.name: Habakkuk
habakkuk.description: Prophet whose questions to God produced the line of faith.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.description: Wrestled with God over the rise of the Babylonians; received the answer that the righteous shall live by faith.

zephaniah.name: Zephaniah
zephaniah.description: Royal-descent prophet of the early reign of Josiah.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.description: Prophesied before Josiah's reforms; foretold the great day of the Lord against Judah and the nations.

obadiah.name: Obadiah
obadiah.description: Shortest book in the Hebrew Bible; vision against Edom.

stops.name: Judah
stops.description: Pronounced doom on Edom for standing by during Jerusalem's fall.

stops.name: Edom
stops.description: Target of his vision — the mountain strongholds of Esau's descendants in the southern desert.

haggai.name: Haggai
haggai.description: Post-exilic prophet whose two-month ministry rebuilt the temple.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.description: Urged Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the people to take up the work on the temple again in 520 BC.

zechariah-prophet.name: Zechariah the prophet
zechariah-prophet.description: Co-prophet with Haggai of the post-exilic temple project.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.description: Received the eight night visions; encouraged the returnees to finish the temple; saw the king on a donkey from afar.

malachi.name: Malachi
malachi.description: Last voice of the Old Testament; promised a coming messenger.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.description: Confronted a community drifting after the rebuilt temple; foretold the messenger to prepare the way.

judas-iscariot.name: Judas Iscariot
judas-iscariot.description: From the band of twelve to a hanged man in the field of blood.

stops.name: Galilee (calling)
stops.description: Chosen as one of the twelve apostles; kept the common purse and stole from it.

stops.name: Jerusalem (the bargain)
stops.description: Went to the chief priests; bargained for thirty pieces of silver.

stops.name: Gethsemane
stops.description: Led the arresting party by torchlight; identified Jesus with a kiss.

stops.name: The temple (return of silver)
stops.description: Flung the thirty pieces of silver into the temple in remorse.

stops.name: The Field of Blood (Akeldama)
stops.description: Hanged himself; the priests bought the potter's field with the blood money he had thrown back.

thomas.name: Thomas
thomas.description: From Galilean fisherman to (by tradition) the apostle to India.

stops.name: Galilee
stops.description: Fisherman called as one of the twelve, nicknamed Didymus — twin.

stops.name: Bethany (Lazarus)
stops.description: Said boldly, 'let us go too, that we may die with him' when Jesus turned toward Lazarus.

stops.name: The upper room
stops.description: Missing on the first resurrection appearance; eight days later confessed, 'my Lord and my God.'

stops.name: Kerala, India (tradition)
stops.description: Tradition has him reaching the Malabar coast of India; the Mar Thoma church still claims him as founder.

felix.name: Felix
felix.description: Roman procurator at Caesarea who heard Paul.

stops.name: Caesarea Maritima
stops.description: Heard Paul's case and reasoned with him about righteousness; left him in prison two years hoping for a bribe.

festus.name: Festus
festus.description: Succeeded Felix; shipped Paul to Rome on his appeal to Caesar.

stops.name: Caesarea Maritima
stops.description: Heard Paul's case; presented him to Agrippa; arranged transport to Rome.

stops.name: Jerusalem
stops.description: Went up within three days of arriving in his province; refused to transfer the case there.

agrippa.name: Agrippa
agrippa.description: Last Herodian ruler; heard Paul's most personal defense.

stops.name: Rome
stops.description: Raised in the imperial court at Rome.

stops.name: Caesarea Philippi
stops.description: Capital of his northern territories of Iturea and Trachonitis.

stops.name: Caesarea Maritima
stops.description: Came on a state visit with Bernice; heard Paul's defense and said he was almost persuaded to be a Christian.

mary.name: Mary
mary.description: From the Annunciation in Nazareth to the upper room at Pentecost.

stops.name: Nazareth (Annunciation)
stops.description: Received Gabriel's announcement: you will conceive and bear a son and shall call his name Jesus.

stops.name: Ein Karem
stops.description: Visited her cousin Elizabeth in the hill country; sang the Magnificat — 'my soul magnifies the Lord.'

stops.name: Bethlehem
stops.description: Bore Jesus in a manger; the shepherds came to see and the angels sang on the hillside.

stops.name: Jerusalem (the temple)
stops.description: Presented Jesus on the eighth day; Simeon foretold a sword that would pierce her own soul.

stops.name: Egypt
stops.description: Fled with Joseph and the child by night to escape Herod's massacre.

stops.name: Nazareth (Jesus's youth)
stops.description: Raised Jesus here; kept these things and pondered them in her heart.

stops.name: Jerusalem (the lost boy)
stops.description: Found the twelve-year-old Jesus among the teachers in the temple after three anxious days.

stops.name: Cana
stops.description: At the wedding feast told Jesus the wine had run out — 'do whatever he tells you.'

stops.name: Capernaum
stops.description: Came down with his brothers seeking him; sent in word but did not interrupt his teaching.

stops.name: Golgotha
stops.description: Stood at the foot of the cross with the beloved disciple; was given into his care by Jesus's last words.

stops.name: Jerusalem (the upper room)
stops.description: Gathered with the disciples in the upper room after the ascension, devoted to prayer.

stops.name: Ephesus (tradition)
stops.description: Tradition places her later years under John's care in Ephesus.
